title: Intracranial EEG from 9 adults during a memory-guided actions experiment (preprocessed epochs, Moraresku et al.)
description: Preprocessed stereo-EEG epochs from nine patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a delayed memory-guided action task at the Motol Epilepsy Center in Prague. The data are bipolar-referenced and notch-filtered, with 170 epochs per patient time-locked to encoding onset. Recordings cover the inferior parietal lobule, ventral temporal cortex and hippocampus, and were used to study interactions between the dorsal and ventral visual streams during working memory. This BIDS derivative re-packages the authors' Zenodo release without further processing.
methods_description: Stereo-EEG was recorded with 11-15 semi-rigid depth electrodes per patient (DIXI Medical) using Quantum NeuroWorks amplifiers at 2048 Hz. Data were downsampled to 512 Hz, notch filtered at 50 Hz and harmonics, and bipolar-referenced between adjacent contacts. Contacts that were faulty or in the seizure onset zone were removed, and data were epoched from -2 to 7.898 s around encoding onset. In each trial of the delayed memory-guided action task, patients encoded the positions of two objects, waited through a delay, and then reached with a joystick to the remembered position. The task was presented with PsychoPy3, and task and iEEG were synchronized by TTL pulses. Contact positions were obtained from post-implantation CT co-registered to MRI and normalized to MNI space with SPM12.
